name: Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation
title: Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation
answer: Data loss prevention and sanitisation covers the controls that stop sensitive information leaving an organisation and the processes that strip or mask it when data must be shared, reused or tested. In an AI context the scope widens to include prompts, training sets, embeddings, model outputs and logs, because each can carry personal data, trade secrets or regulated records. It sits alongside classification, access control and retention, and it is a routine part of AI security audits and enterprise enablement rather than a separate discipline.

sections.body: Data loss prevention and sanitisation covers the controls that stop sensitive information leaving an organisation and the processes that strip or mask it when data must be shared, reused or tested. In an AI context the scope widens to include prompts, training sets, embeddings, model outputs and logs, because each can carry personal data, trade secrets or regulated records. It sits alongside classification, access control and retention, and it is a routine part of AI security audits and enterprise enablement rather than a separate discipline.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on a mix of endpoint and network agents, cloud access security brokers, email and web gateways, and data classification engines that tag content as it is created or moved. For AI systems the same controls are extended to model gateways, prompt logging pipelines, vector stores and training data lakes, often through policy engines that inspect traffic before it reaches a model. Identity and access management supplies the user context, and a central policy console usually holds the rules that the other components enforce.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Practitioners start with discovery, using pattern matching, fingerprinting and machine learning classifiers to find where sensitive data actually lives and how it flows. They then define policies that block, quarantine, encrypt, redact or tokenise data depending on its class and destination, and they test those policies against realistic scenarios before enforcement. Sanitisation for AI adds techniques such as de-identification, synthetic data generation, differential privacy and output filtering, with audit logs kept so that each decision can be reconstructed later.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Ownership usually sits with security, privacy and legal teams jointly, because a single incident can trigger breach notification duties, contractual claims and regulatory scrutiny.Provenance matters as much as prevention: teams record where data came from, what licence or consent covers it, what transformations were applied and who approved each exception. Records of that kind support audits, subject access requests and defences when a claim is made.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Expect tighter coupling between data loss prevention and AI governance as regulators ask for evidence that training and prompt data were lawfully obtained and properly minimised. Classifiers will keep improving, but so will the difficulty of separating sensitive content from ordinary business text, and shadow AI use will remain a practical gap. The likely direction is policy expressed once and enforced across endpoints, cloud, model gateways and agent workflows, with provenance metadata travelling alongside the data itself.
